newsitem.title: USA: US ag attache lowers Brazil 96/97 soybean forecast.
newsitem.headline: US ag attache lowers Brazil 96/97 soybean forecast.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache posted at the U.S. embassy in Sao Paulo lowered his forecast for Brazil's 1996/97 soybean production by almost two percent to 26.5 million tonnes due to prolonged drought in Rio Grande do Sul, one of Brazil's key soybean growing areas.

"While rains fell over this state last weekend, they came too late to reverse the effects of this drought, which is expected to lower production to 5.2 million (tonnes), down over 13 percent from post's last estimate," the attache wrote in a report dated May 1 that was released in Washington Tuesday.

The attache also raised his forecast for Brazil 1996/97 soybean exports to 7.0 million tonnes from 6.0 million tonnes seen previously, citing high international prices and the removal of a value-added tax as two reasons for the gain.

Because of the forecast export rise, the attache lowered his crush estimate by five percent to 19 million tonnes. Soybean meal and soybean oil output were pegged at 15 million and 3.58 million tonnes, respectively, down almost five percent for both.
Soybean meal and soybean oil exports were also lowered, reflecting the lower crush. Soybean imports were seen rising to 1.1 million tonnes from 600,000 tonnes previously estimated.

On soybean production, the attache said unexpectedly high yields in the state of Goias will partially offset the drop in production in Rio Grande do Sul. He raised his forecast for soybean production in Goias to 2.5 million tonnes, up over 13 percent from a prior estimate.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.

In its World Agricultural Supply and Demand Report released April 11, USDA pegged Brazil's 1996/97 soybean crop at 27.00 million tonnes and exports at 5.2 million tonnes. Soybean meal production was seen at 16.19 million tonnes while soyoil output was pegged at 3.85 million tonnes.
